record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For a sequence f: Z -> R, define the discrete centered one-dimensional Hardy-Littlewood maximal function by M f(n) = sup_{r>=0} (2r+1)^{-1} sum_{k=-r}^{r} |f(n+k)|, where r ranges over nonnegative integers. If f has bounded variation on Z, must the sharp inequality Var(M f) <= Var(f) hold? If not, can Temur's known constant 294912004 in Var(M f) <= 294912004 Var(f) be substantially improved?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a sequence $f:\mathbb{Z}	o\mathbb{R}$, define the discrete centered one-dimensional Hardy–Littlewood maximal function by
$$ Mf(n) \;=\; \sup_{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}}  rac{1}{2r+1}\sum_{k=-r}^{r} |f(n+k)|, \qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}. $$
For a sequence $g:\mathbb{Z}	o\mathbb{R}$, define its total variation by
$$ \operatorname{Var}(g) \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |g(n+1)-g(n)|, $$
and say that $g$ has bounded variation if $\operatorname{Var}(g)<\infty$.

It is known that there exists a finite constant $C$ such that for every $f:\mathbb{Z}	o\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation,
$$ \operatorname{Var}(Mf) \;\le\; C\,\operatorname{Var}(f), $$
and one admissible value of $C$ is $C=294{,}912{,}004$.

(a) Decide whether the sharp inequality
$$ \operatorname{Var}(Mf) \;\le\; \operatorname{Var}(f) $$
holds for every $f:\mathbb{Z}	o\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation.

(b) If (a) fails, determine whether the constant $C=294{,}912{,}004$ in the above inequality can be substantially improved, and find the best (or a substantially smaller) admissible constant.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) on the one-dimensional centered maximal operator has established sharp variation inequalities in special cases (e.g., indicator functions and certain simple functions in both continuous and discrete settings), but the general sharp inequality Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) for arbitrary BV sequences on Z, and the question of substantially improving Temur's constant 294,912,004, do not appear to have been settled in full generality. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The One-Dimensional Centred Maximal Function Diminishes the Variation of Indicator Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp variation bound proved for indicator functions in continuous and discrete settings; general BV case not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) established only for indicator functions, not for general BV sequences.

status_evidence.title: Variation of the one-dimensional centered maximal operator on simple functions with gaps between pieces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent partial progress for simple functions with gaps; general case not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress only; full sharp inequality remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: Sharp inequalities for the variation (Temur)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes Var(Mf) ≤ C Var(f) with a large explicit constant in the discrete centered setting.
status_evidence.claim: Temur's large constant is current best general bound; not known to be substantially improved.
